# pfmatch

Matching **990-PF grant recipients** (Form 990-PF Part XIV Table 3a,
“grants paid during the year”) to the **IRS Business Master File** to
recover recipient EINs.

The record-linkage machinery is
[`npmatch`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/npmatch):
normalization, blocking, comparison, hierarchical scoring, the veto
layer, and YES / MAYBE / NO tiering are all used unchanged. This package
holds only what is specific to the 990-PF grant context.

## Install

``` r
# npmatch first — pfmatch Imports it
install.packages("../npmatch", repos = NULL, type = "source")
install.packages(".",          repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

## Use

Four stages, or one call:

``` r
library(pfmatch)

res <- pf_run(grants = "inputs", bmf = ".../bmf_2026_01_processed.csv")

# or stage by stage, when you want to cache between them
prep <- pf_prepare(grants, dedup = "fuzzy")        # read -> repair -> scope -> dedup
ref  <- pf_reference(bmf)                          # build or load the cached bundle
lnk  <- pf_link(prep, ref, batch_size = 25000)     # cascade -> self-guard -> propagate
adj  <- pf_adjudicate(lnk, bmf)                    # the review sheet
```

| stage | does | key functions |
|----|----|----|
| [`pf_prepare()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_prepare.md) | read grants, repair name-in-street, standardize the recipient-status field, decide scope, collapse to distinct recipient identities | [`pf_read_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_read_grants.md), [`pf_prepare_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_prepare_grants.md), [`pf_standardize_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_standardize_status.md), [`pf_dedup()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dedup.md), [`pf_recipients()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recipients.md) |
| [`pf_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_reference.md) | read + normalize the BMF, name frequency, token IDF, blocking index, acronym/prefix keys — cached, and excluded from match timings | [`pf_build_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_reference.md) |
| [`pf_link()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_link.md) | the staged blocking cascade in checkpointed batches, self-match guard, then propagate each identity’s result to every grant row | [`pf_staged_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_staged_passes.md), [`pf_recovery_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recovery_passes.md), [`pf_run_batches()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_run_batches.md), [`pf_propagate_matches()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_propagate_matches.md) |
| [`pf_adjudicate()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_adjudicate.md) | candidate sheet with BMF and foundation context, optional purpose tiebreak | [`pf_candidate_frame()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_candidate_frame.md), [`pf_build_org_text()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_org_text.md), [`pf_purpose_tiebreak()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose_tiebreak.md) |

Results are summarized by
[`pf_report()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_report.md),
[`pf_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_status.md),
and
[`pf_crosstab()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_crosstab.md).

## Repository layout

    R/               the package
    data/            nteev2.rda — the only bundled data (built by data-raw/)
    data-raw/        make-nteev2.R
    inputs/          grant CSVs, 990 Part III extracts, NTEE source files  (not shipped)
    data-dev/        derived artifacts, caches, checkpoints                (not shipped)
    dev/             benchmarks, probes, findings                          (not shipped)

`inputs/` was called `data/` until the package skeleton was added; it
holds 600 MB+ of source files and had to give up the name to R’s
reserved `data/`.

## What is specific to this problem

### 1. `R/recipient-type.R` — standardizing `SIGOCPYRFSTA`

Column (c) of the grants table asks the filer for the “foundation status
of recipient” and the IRS supplies no controlled vocabulary. Across
155,000 sample grants the field carries **~1,400 distinct spellings** of
about eight concepts.

[`pf_standardize_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_standardize_status.md)
is a rule cascade, not a lookup table, so unseen spellings land in the
right bucket. Two normalizations do most of the work:

- **section collapsing** — `501(c)(3)`, `501C 3`, `501 C 3`, `501c3` all
  become the single token `501C3`; likewise `509A1`, `170B1A`, `4942J3`.
- **de-spacing** — every pattern is also matched against a space-free
  copy of the string, so `PUB CHAR`, `PUBLIC CH`, and
  `OTHERPUBLICCHARITY` are all caught by one pattern.

Order matters: operating foundations are tested before the generic
501(c)(3) rules (an operating foundation *is* a c3 but is emphatically
not a public charity), and government before the bare-`PUBLIC` fallback
(so “PUBLIC UNIVERSITY” does not become a public charity).

| level             | share of 155k |
|-------------------|---------------|
| `public_charity`  | 70.5%         |
| `other_unknown`   | 20.6%         |
| `nonprofit_other` | 4.3%          |
| `individual`      | 3.6%          |
| `foundation_pf`   | 1.1%          |

Coverage is 98.6%; the 1.4% residual is text that answers a different
question (“PAID”, “CASH”, “VARIOUS”, “ACTIVE”, “SEE GENERAL
EXPLANATION”). Use `pf_status_audit(x, detail = "unrecognized")` to see
what a new extract still misses before trusting the split.

A finer `recipient_type_detail` is carried alongside, because
`other_unknown` mixes cases that behave very differently — `government`
and `foreign` can never be in the BMF, while `blank` and `unrecognized`
are usually organizations the filer simply did not code. **Only the
detail level drives scope**
([`pf_oos_details()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_oos_details.md)).

Two judgment calls worth knowing about:

- **`NC`** is the standard shorthand for a *non-charity* recipient — the
  filers who spell it out write “NC: NON-EXEMPT”. It says what the
  recipient is *not*, so it is not promoted to “nonprofit (other)”, but
  it stays **in scope**: a 501(c)(4) or a taxable entity may still hold
  a BMF row.
- **Equivalency determinations** are how a US foundation grants to a
  foreign org with no IRS ruling, so they are classified `foreign` and
  held out of the match.

### 2. `R/prepare.R` — recipient name and address

The data dictionary settles the name-field question. There are three
columns:

- `SIGOCPYRPNAM` — “Name of Grantee — **Person**”
- `SIGOCPYRBNBN1` — “Name of Grantee — **Business** Line 1”
- `SIGOCPYRBNBN2` — “Name of Grantee — **Business** Line 2”

So `BNBN1`/`BNBN2` are a two-line **wrap of one name**, not a main name
and a DBA — confirming the working assumption. `PNAM` and `BNBN1` never
co-occur (0 of 155,000 rows carry both), so the recipient name is a
straight coalesce.

`PNAM` is **not** a usable individual flag: filers routinely put
organizations in it (“World Central Kitchen”, “Surfrider Foundation”),
which is why scope is decided from `SIGOCPYRFSTA` instead.

Line 2, when present, is one of four things and each is handled
separately:

| line 2 is | n (5k sample) | handling |
|----|----|----|
| a genuine continuation | 2,047 | joined onto line 1 as an alternate name |
| a duplicate of line 1 | 983 | dropped |
| a care-of / attention line | 735 | dropped (address data in a name field) |
| an FBO beneficiary | 27 | dropped, trailing `FBO` stripped from line 1 |

The joined continuation is carried in npmatch’s `dba` slot. That is a
deliberate reuse rather than a claim that it is a DBA: `np_compare()`
scores the full name/DBA cross-product and keeps the best, so a record
can match on either the truncated line-1 form or the complete one —
whichever the BMF happens to hold. It earns its keep: the
`exact-name-dba` pass resolves 86 YES on the 5k sample.

Other handling: 4-digit ZIPs are repaired (a dropped New-England leading
zero), spelled-out state names are folded to postal codes, and a state
value that is not a US postal jurisdiction marks the record foreign.
`SIGOCAFFRFACO` (country) is in the schema but empty throughout the
sample, so foreign detection has to come from the state field.

`looks_personal` is a diagnostic only and never drives scope: a 2-3
token name with no institutional token *and* a positive person signal (a
single-letter initial, or a common given name). It fires on 0.7% of YES
matches and 18% of out-of-sample rows, which is the right direction.

### 3. `R/match.R` — the cascade

Full walkthrough in **`dev/CASCADE.md`**: what is compared, the scoring
formula, all eleven passes, the vetoes, and how a grant lands in YES /
MAYBE / NO. The short version:

**Both sides carry two name slots**, so name similarity is the best of a
cross-product — `max(name×name, name×dba, dba×name, dba×dba)`. The query
`dba` is `recip_name_alt`, the untruncated line1+line2 form. Address is
not one comparison either: seven location signals are emitted and the
geo score takes the strongest, never a sum.

    score = 0.60 · name  +  0.40 · geo

    geo   = max( 1.00·zip9,  0.95·street,  0.90·zip5,  0.90·pobox,
                 0.55·zip3,  0.50·city,    0.20·state )

Taking the `max` means correlated address fields cannot double-count and
a wrong city cannot pull down a ZIP-confirmed match. Fuzzy similarities
are floored to 0 below `jw_threshold` (0.85) — reclin2’s `threshold=` is
the Winkler prefix *boost*, not a cutoff, so unrelated strings otherwise
leak ~0.5 into every score.

Eleven passes run cheapest-first and **a query resolved to YES leaves
the pending set**, so expensive passes only see the residue. Stage A
(exact, state-blocked) resolves the bulk on a few thousand candidates;
stages B–D spend two orders of magnitude more candidates on the tail.

Tiering is `score ≥ 0.78 → YES`, `≥ 0.65 → MAYBE`, else `NO`, with two
demotions from YES to MAYBE: a **margin under 0.05** to the runner-up
(an ambiguity brake — something else is nearly as good), and a **soft
veto**. The soft vetoes that matter here are `affiliate_suffix`
(candidate ends FOUNDATION / ENDOWMENT / AUXILIARY / BOOSTERS and the
query does not) and `government_entity`.

> **These thresholds are npmatch defaults, fitted on SAM/USASpending —
> not on 990-PF data.** What is worth re-tuning, what the current label
> set can support, and why tier boundaries cannot be tuned on MAYBE-only
> labels: `dev/OPTIMIZATION-PLAN.md`.

### 3a. Two pass configurations

**[`pf_staged_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_staged_passes.md)
is the production cascade** (state-blocked bulk plus a cheap cross-state
exact sweep) and
**[`pf_default_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_default_passes.md)
is the state-free measurement baseline**. On 5,000 grants the staged
`lean` configuration is 1.48x faster, uses 2.0x fewer candidate pairs,
and returns 13 *more* YES matches. See `dev/SCALE-PLAN.md` for the full
comparison.

The single most efficient pass is `A1`, which blocks on **name + ZIP5
with no state key**: 1,834 matches from 8,285 candidates. It is also
what makes state blocking safe, because it catches the “filer typed the
wrong state” cases (right city, right ZIP, wrong two-letter code)
without any cross-state sweep.

The unblocked *token* sweep is off by default (`sweep = "lean"`).
Measured, it generated 59% of all candidate pairs and produced **zero**
additional YES matches — its only product is extra MAYBE candidates.
Turn it on with `sweep = "full"` when filling the adjudication queue
matters more than runtime.

### 3b. The state-free baseline and why it exists

npmatch’s default cascade blocks every pass on `state` and only opens up
to a cross-state token pass at the end. That is right when query and
reference are the same establishment; it is wrong here, because a New
York foundation routinely funds a California charity and the address the
filer types is whatever was on the check. Every pass in
[`pf_default_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_default_passes.md)
is state-free:

| pass             | criterion                                        |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `exact-name`     | name == name, any state                          |
| `exact-name-dba` | name == dba, any state                           |
| `exact-dba-name` | dba == name, any state                           |
| `exact-dba-dba`  | dba == dba, any state                            |
| `token-any`      | shared distinctive token (IDF-pruned), any state |

“No blocking” cannot mean a full cross product — 5,000 grants against
1.9M BMF rows is 9.6 billion pairs. What is dropped is *geographic*
blocking. Candidates are still generated by exact name keys and by a
shared distinctive name token, which is a recall device rather than a
geographic constraint. State is used only downstream, as scoring
evidence.

[`pf_build_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_reference.md)
does the one-time BMF work (read, normalize, name frequency, token IDF,
blocking index) and caches it, so it is excluded from the match timings.
[`pf_match_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_match_grants.md)
times **only** the cascade.

### 4. `R/report.R` — the four-way outcome

- `YES` — one candidate cleared the auto-accept threshold with a clear
  lead
- `MAYBE` — candidates surfaced but need adjudication (below threshold,
  a near-tie with the runner-up, or a soft veto)
- `NO` — no candidate surfaced, or the best one scored below the review
  floor
- `OOS` — out of sample: a natural person, a government unit, or a
  foreign organization. Nothing to find, so not counted as a miss.

[`pf_report()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_report.md)
prints the outcome split, the outcome x recipient-type crosstab,
geographic-agreement diagnostics, the per-pass cascade table, and the
runtime;
[`pf_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_status.md),
[`pf_crosstab()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_crosstab.md),
and
[`pf_geo_agreement()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_geo_agreement.md)
return the frames.

### 5. `R/dyads.R` — EIN dyads

A grant reported to `EAGLE RANCH` may have been paid to
`EAGLE RANCH FOUNDATION`. When both are candidates, the margin brake in
§3 fires on a runner-up that is *the same body under a second EIN* —
median margin on affected grants is exactly **0.000**, a grant held back
for tying with itself.

[`pf_build_dyads()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_dyads.md)
reads Schedule A Part I line 12g and Schedule R Part II disclosures
(2009–2024) and classifies each disclosed pair as `substitutable` or
merely `related`. `pf_link(dyads = )` then collapses substitutable
candidates *within one grant’s candidate list* before selection and
re-runs the tiering: **704 MAYBE grants become YES on the 50k run, with
nothing moving into NO.**

Two rules are not negotiable, both learned the hard way:

- **Direct edges only, never a transitive closure.** Connected
  components over the disclosure graph produce a single component of
  66,973 EINs across 56 states.
- **Substitution requires exclusivity.** A bare Schedule A edge gave the
  *YMCA Retirement Fund* 905 “substitutable” partners — it supports 907
  local YMCAs.

`dev/DYAD-FINDINGS.md` for the evidence, `dev/CLUSTER-FINDINGS.md` for
the negative result that shaped the design.

## Benchmarks and development

``` bash
PF_SET=1k Rscript dev/run-test-match.R      # the five 1,000-row files
PF_SET=50k Rscript dev/run-test-match.R
PF_SET=100k Rscript dev/run-test-match.R
Rscript dev/run-full-file.R                 # checkpointed production run
```

The first run builds `data-dev/BMF-REFERENCE-BUNDLE.rds` (~5 min, 1.3
GB) and reuses it thereafter. Set `NPMATCH_DIR` / `PFMATCH_DIR` to
relocate.

`dev/` scripts use
[`devtools::load_all()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/load_all.html)
rather than [`library(pfmatch)`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html),
so they can reach internal and unexported functions. They are not part
of the package.

Planning documents: `dev/PACKAGE-PLAN.md` (what packaging still owes),
`dev/NPMATCH-PROMOTION-PLAN.md` (three modules to move upstream, and one
npmatch defect this project found).

## Results, 5,000-grant sample

See `dev/BENCHMARK-NOTES.md` for the full read-out and what it implies
for the next round.

## Audits

`dev/AUDIT-FINDINGS.md` reports three 100-case manual audits of the NO,
OOS, and MAYBE tiers, with per-case verdicts in
`dev/maybe-verdicts.csv`. Short version: the NO tier is mostly real
nonprofits we failed to reach (13 of 15 web-confirmed EINs are in the
BMF), the OOS flag is wrong 24% of the time because column (c) describes
the beneficiary rather than the payee, and 63% of MAYBE cases contain
the correct EIN in the top five candidates.

# Package index

## Run the pipeline

End to end.
[`pf_run()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_run.md)
is the whole thing; the staged functions are the same work with the
seams exposed.

- [`pf_pipeline`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_pipeline.md)
  : End-to-end wrappers
- [`pf_run()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_run.md)
  : Run the whole pipeline
- [`pf_run_batches()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_run_batches.md)
  : Run the cascade over a large grant file in checkpointed batches
- [`pf_link()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_link.md)
  : Stage 3 — run the cascade and propagate to grant rows
- [`pf_batch_doc`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_batch_doc.md)
  : Stage 6 — checkpointed batch driver for the full grant file
- [`pf_batch_report()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_batch_report.md)
  : Summarize a batched run

## Stage 1 — read and prepare grants

Parse Part XIV Table 3a, standardize the uncontrolled recipient-status
field, resolve the two-line recipient name, and decide what is in scope.

- [`pf_prepare()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_prepare.md)
  : Stage 1 — read, repair, scope, and collapse to identities
- [`pf_read_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_read_grants.md)
  : Read and prepare the sample grant CSVs
- [`pf_prepare_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_prepare_grants.md)
  : Prepare a raw 990-PF grants extract
- [`pf_recover_name_from_street()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recover_name_from_street.md)
  : Recover a recipient name typed into the street field
- [`pf_recipient_type`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recipient_type.md)
  : Standardize the 990-PF recipient foundation-status field
  (SIGOCPYRFSTA)
- [`pf_standardize_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_standardize_status.md)
  : Standardize SIGOCPYRFSTA into recipient types
- [`pf_status_audit()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_status_audit.md)
  : Audit the standardization
- [`pf_schedule_a_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_schedule_a_status.md)
  : Schedule A Part I public-charity status flags
- [`pf_is_placeholder()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_is_placeholder.md)
  : Flag grant rows whose recipient is a pointer to an attachment
- [`pf_placeholder_pattern()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_placeholder_pattern.md)
  : Patterns that mark a recipient name as a pointer rather than a name
- [`pf_attached`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_attached.md)
  : Returns that do not report grants directly
- [`pf_attached_report()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_attached_report.md)
  : Report on returns that do not itemize their grants

## Stage 2 — collapse to recipient identities

Repeated grant rows become one identity, so the cascade scores each
recipient once rather than once per grant.

- [`pf_dedup_doc`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dedup_doc.md)
  : Collapse grant rows to distinct recipient identities
- [`pf_dedup()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dedup.md)
  : Deduplicate grant recipients
- [`pf_recipients()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recipients.md)
  : The distinct recipient frame to actually match
- [`pf_dedup_report()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dedup_report.md)
  : Report on a dedup run
- [`pf_propagate_matches()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_propagate_matches.md)
  : Propagate a match back from identities to grant rows
- [`pf_group_siblings()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_group_siblings.md)
  : Federated siblings from the BMF group exemption

## Stage 3 — the reference

Compile the BMF side: layers, name variants, enrichment text.

- [`pf_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_reference.md)
  : Stage 2 — the BMF reference bundle
- [`pf_build_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_reference.md)
  : Build the BMF reference once
- [`pf_bmf_augment()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_bmf_augment.md)
  : Append Schedule I alias rows to the BMF
- [`pf_collapse_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_collapse_reference.md)
  : Collapse reference rows the matcher cannot tell apart
- [`pf_partition_reference()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_partition.md)
  [`pf_route_queries()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_partition.md)
  [`pf_run_partitioned()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_partition.md)
  : Partition the reference by state, and run the cascade over the
  partition
- [`pf_bmf_context()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_bmf_context.md)
  : Build a compact BMF context table keyed by EIN
- [`pf_text`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_text.md)
  : Organization self-description text, keyed by EIN
- [`pf_build_org_text()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_org_text.md)
  : Build the EIN -\> self-description table
- [`pf_attach_missions()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_attach_missions.md)
  : Attach an external mission table
- [`nteev2`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/nteev2.md)
  : NTEE codes rendered as text

## Stage 4 — the matching cascade

The staged blocking passes and the match itself. See the cascade article
for what each pass does and which cases it clears.

- [`pf_match`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_match.md)
  : Match 990-PF grant recipients to the BMF
- [`pf_match_grants()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_match_grants.md)
  : Run the grant-recipient match
- [`pf_staged_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_staged_passes.md)
  : Staged cascade: state-blocked bulk, then an unblocked residual sweep
- [`pf_recover`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recover.md)
  : Stage 4 — alias and repair passes
- [`pf_recovery_passes()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_recovery_passes.md)
  : Stage 4 recovery passes
- [`pf_add_recovery_keys()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_add_recovery_keys.md)
  : Add acronym and prefix recovery columns to a normalized frame
- [`pf_drop_self_matches()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_drop_self_matches.md)
  : Never match a grant to the foundation that made it
- [`pf_status()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_status.md)
  : Per-grant outcome frame
- [`pf_crosstab()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_crosstab.md)
  : Outcome x recipient-type crosstab
- [`pf_geo_agreement()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_geo_agreement.md)
  : Geographic-agreement diagnostics

## Stage 5 — adjudication

Build the sheet a human or an LLM reviews. There is no safe automatic
acceptance of the MAYBE tier; see `dev/ADJUDICATION-PLAN.md`.

- [`pf_adjudicate()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_adjudicate.md)
  : Stage 4 — build the adjudication sheet
- [`pf_candidate_frame()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_candidate_frame.md)
  : Candidate-level adjudication frame
- [`pf_enrich`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_enrich.md)
  : Enrich match results with BMF context for adjudication
- [`pf_purpose`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose.md)
  : Grant purpose as a tiebreak signal
- [`pf_purpose_tiebreak()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose_tiebreak.md)
  : Break near-ties on grant purpose and filing presence
- [`pf_purpose_is_contentful()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose_is_contentful.md)
  : Does the purpose say anything?
- [`pf_purpose_coverage()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose_coverage.md)
  : IDF-weighted containment of a purpose in a document
- [`pf_purpose_tokens()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_purpose_tokens.md)
  : Tokenize purpose or organization text

## Evaluation against ground truth

Score a configuration instead of arguing about its clear rate: a
clear-rate delta cannot separate recall from false accepts.

- [`pf_evaluate()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_evaluate.md)
  : Score a run against ground truth
- [`pf_consistency()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_consistency.md)
  : Consistency across renderings of one organisation
- [`pf_truth_schema()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_truth_schema.md)
  : Ground-truth table columns
- [`pf_population_id()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_population_id.md)
  : Fingerprint a grant population

## Affiliates, dyads and sibling structure

Parent, chapter and auxiliary relationships — the dominant source of
wrong-but-plausible matches.

- [`pf_affiliation`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_affiliation.md)
  : Affiliated organizations: operating entities and their fundraising
  arms
- [`pf_build_affiliation_links()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_affiliation_links.md)
  : Build the EIN-to-EIN affiliation link table
- [`pf_dyads`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyads.md)
  : Disclosed EIN dyads: substitutable pairs and merely related ones
- [`pf_build_dyads()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_build_dyads.md)
  : Build the dyad table
- [`pf_dyad_annotate()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_annotate.md)
  : Attach dyad context to a match result
- [`pf_dyad_collapse()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_collapse.md)
  : Collapse substitutable candidates before selection
- [`pf_dyad_config()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_config.md)
  : Dyad collapse settings
- [`pf_dyad_lookup()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_lookup.md)
  : Look up the dyad class for pairs of EINs
- [`pf_dyad_sources()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_sources.md)
  : Default locations of the linkid dyad extracts
- [`pf_dyad_summary()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_dyad_summary.md)
  : Summarise a dyad table
- [`pf_cluster_arms()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_cluster_arms.md)
  : Group a candidate list into operating/arm clusters
- [`pf_arm_core()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_arm_core.md)
  : The shared core of an organization name
- [`pf_arm_order()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_arm_order.md)
  : Order the members of an operating/arm cluster
- [`pf_is_arm()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_is_arm.md)
  : Is this name a fundraising or support arm?

## Source data

Build the grant file from the NCCS e-file extracts, and Schedule I
aliases.

- [`pf_efilepf_years()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf.md)
  [`pf_efilepf_table()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf.md)
  [`pf_efilepf_dir()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf.md)
  : 990-PF Part XV grants paid, direct from the NCCS e-file extracts
- [`pf_efilepf_build()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf_build.md)
  : Build the rebuilt grant file from the downloaded extracts
- [`pf_efilepf_download()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf_download.md)
  : Download the e-file 990-PF grants-paid extracts
- [`pf_efilepf_map()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf_map.md)
  : The e-file to GTDC column mapping
- [`pf_efilepf_url()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_efilepf_url.md)
  : URL for one year of the e-file 990-PF grants-paid extract
- [`pf_schedi`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_schedi.md)
  : Form 990 Schedule I as an alias source for the BMF
- [`pf_schedi_alias()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_schedi_alias.md)
  : Read the alias table, one row per (EIN, name)
- [`pf_schedi_build()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_schedi_build.md)
  : Load the extracts into DuckDB and reduce them to an alias table
- [`pf_schedi_download()`](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/pfmatch/reference/pf_schedi_download.md)
  : Download the Schedule I extracts
